title: How to find and book flights, hotels and more for AHR Expo 2027
summary: Plan your AHR Expo 2027 trip to Chicago with practical advice on hotels, airports, McCormick Place transit, winter packing, agendas, meetings, and meals.
body_markdown:
AHR Expo 2027 show runs Jan. 25–27 at McCormick Place in Chicago, bringing HVACR professionals together for exhibits, education, and business conversations.1 Planning has to cover more than a flight and a room: January weather can complicate a commute, a large show floor could benefit from advance research, and an unstructured demo can consume valuable time without actually answering the question that brought you there.


This guide helps build the trip around exactly these considerations. It covers where to stay, how to reach the venue from either Chicago airport, how to divide the show days, and how to turn product conversations into decisions your team can use.


### Key takeaways


- On-campus hotels offer covered access to McCormick Place, while official show hotels include show-day shuttle service. Decide how much winter exposure and schedule variability you can accept before comparing hotel rooms.3,6
- Use the exhibitor directory, floor plan, and My Show Planner to group visits and protect time for technical questions.1,2
- Navan Edge can take care of flights, hotels and even restaurant bookings, all in one chat thread, that also considers connected loyalty programs to earn you the most rewarding stays.
- Pack for the route, as well as the venue itself. Chicago’s January climate normals are below freezing, and snow this time of year is common 5
- Record the product, question, owner, and next step after each important conversation instead of relying on a stack of brochures.


## What is AHR Expo 2027, and who is it for?


AHR Expo 2027 is designed for HVACR professionals across engineering, contracting, manufacturing, distribution, architecture, facilities, utilities, education, and related fields. International Exposition Company produces the show; ASHRAE and AHRI are co-sponsors.1


The event takes place at McCormick Place, 2301 S. Martin Luther King Drive, from Monday, Jan. 25 through Wednesday, Jan. 27. Show hours are 10 a.m.–6 p.m. Monday and Tuesday and 10 a.m.–4 p.m. Wednesday.1


An engineer comparing component performance needs a different agenda from a facilities leader evaluating an upgrade path or a distributor looking for new lines. Start by defining the decision you would like to make after the show, then identify the people and evidence needed to make it.


## Is AHR Expo 2027 worth the trip?


AHR may be worth attending if you need to compare equipment in person, question multiple suppliers efficiently, understand how a new system fits an existing facility, or meet partners who influence a specification or rollout.


Your plan might look like this:


- Name two or three current projects or technical questions.
- List the manufacturers, product categories, or specialists relevant to each one.
- Define what you will bring back: a comparison, a shortlist, a recommendation, or a set of follow-up tests.
- Identify meetings that would otherwise require separate trips or calls.


This focus helps shape a work plan you can assess. It also gives you a filter when an interesting booth or session competes with something you’ve scheduled.

## How do you get from Chicago’s airports to McCormick Place?


Chicago O’Hare (ORD) and Midway (MDW) both connect to the CTA rail system. The most useful route depends on your hotel, luggage, arrival hour, and tolerance for transfers.


**Starting point**


**Public-transit route**


**When to consider a car**


O’Hare


Take the Blue Line from the airport and transfer at Clark/Lake to a southbound Green Line train. Cermak–McCormick Place is two blocks from the West Building.4


Heavy equipment, an arrival outside your comfortable transit window, or a hotel poorly served by the route.


Midway


Take the Orange Line to Roosevelt, transfer to the elevated Green Line, and ride one stop south to Cermak–McCormick Place.4


The same luggage and timing considerations apply; compare the route to your hotel rather than the venue alone.


Downtown hotel


Metra Electric stops inside McCormick Place’s Grand Concourse; the Green Line and event hotel shuttles provide other options.3,4


A scheduled car can help when several colleagues travel together or a fixed meeting leaves little margin.


For rideshare pickup after the show, McCormick Place advises using the West Building’s Gate 40.4 Confirm the exact pickup point in the venue signage and app, because convention traffic can make curbside coordination difficult.


## How should you set an AHR Expo travel budget?


One way to build a budget is by dividing into categories


Fixed costs:


Airfare or rail


Four hotel nights if you arrive Sunday and depart Thursday


Ground transport


Registration


Meals outside the event


Any changeable-ticket premium your policy allows.


Add separate lines for the following if relevant:


Client meals


Any hosted meetings


Shipping materials,


Checked equipment


For lodging, compare the total terms as well as the nightly rate. Taxes, cancellation deadlines, and the cost of reaching the venue can change the real trip cost. If your schedule is still fluid, flexibility may be worth more than a small nominal saving.


The same principle applies to the itinerary. When you[book a conference trip](https://navan.com/blog/edge/how-to-book-a-conference-trip) , avoid choosing the earliest possible arrival if a delay would impact your first commitment.


## How should you plan the three show days?


AHR provides My Show Planner for bookmarking exhibitors, viewing the interactive floor plan, searching educational sessions, and building a personal agenda. The organizer says the event app is expected around December.1 Check the live tools again shortly before travel because exhibitor details and schedules can change.


You could focus each day as follows:


- **Monday, Jan. 25, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.:** Orient yourself, complete the first priority visits, and confirm later meetings. Use early demos to refine the questions you ask competing suppliers.
- **Tuesday, Jan. 26, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.:** Put longer technical discussions and scheduled partner meetings here. It is the full middle day, so carve out a break rather than running continuously.
- **Wednesday, Jan. 27, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.:** Resolve open comparisons, revisit the strongest candidates, and collect the contact details needed for follow-up. The earlier close makes a late-day airport dash less forgiving.1


Avoid scheduling back to back for a full day. A large trade show can create great opportunities for unplanned conversations.


## What should you pack for Chicago in January?


National Weather Service climate normals for Chicago show the January high at 31.6°F, the low at 18.8°F, and monthly snowfall at 11.3 inches.5 Check the short-rekange forecast before departure.


For the likely mix of cold sidewalks and heated halls, consider bringing:


- An insulated, wind-resistant outer layer that is easy to remove indoors.
- Weather-resistant shoes with traction, plus conference shoes if you prefer to change.
- Warm socks, gloves, and a compact layer for the airport or platform.
- A light bag that leaves room for notes while avoiding unnecessary sample weight.
- Charging gear and an external battery for the event app and meeting notes.
- Any measurement, compatibility, or procurement questions in an offline file.


Closed, comfortable shoes are also practical around operating equipment and long exhibit-floor days. If a booth visit involves special protective requirements, confirm those with the exhibitor before traveling.


## Tips for networking on the AHR Expo exhibit floor


Start with the organizer’s directory and group priority booths by location.2 For each important visit, write the question you need answered and the evidence that would make the answer useful: a performance range, installation constraint, integration detail, service model, or reference application.


A simple booth note can contain four fields:


- Claim made
- Evidence offered
- Unresolved question
- Next owner


Fill it in immediately after the conversation so later comparisons are more reliable than collecting literature without context.


Ask before photographing a display or slide. AHR’s policy says photography or video of an exhibitor’s booth, products, or personnel is not permitted without that exhibitor’s permission.1 If you need a visual record for your team, request an approved image or spec sheet.


### Who to meet at AHR Expo?


Useful introductions begin with a real problem. Instead of asking what someone does, briefly explain the system, project stage, or constraint you are working through. That gives the other person something specific to respond to.


Consider three kinds of meeting: a peer who has operated a similar system, a supplier who can address a current requirement, and a partner involved in implementation or maintenance. After each substantive conversation, agree on one next step and when it should happen, and be sure to send the follow-up while the context is still clear in your mind.


## Where can you eat near McCormick Place?


Depending on the meal type, group size, there are no shortage of venues for dinner.


Navan Edge can also help you find and book restaurant reservations through the same chat you book your flights and hotel. Here are some recommendations


- **Apolonia:** A contemporary Mediterranean restaurant at 105 E. Cermak Road. Its proximity makes it a practical choice for a sit-down meal near the venue, and it offers personalized events.7
- **Chicago Firehouse Restaurant:** A South Loop option with private-dining spaces, including a room equipped for small business meetings. Consider it when the conversation needs more structure than a quick table.8
- **Gino’s East South Loop:** Offers group-event space and can accommodate a larger team gathering. Confirm the current format and capacity for your date directly with the restaurant.9


For an important client dinner, reserve before the trip and leave enough time to return to the hotel. A late meal after a full day on the floor can undermine the next morning’s priorities.


## What to do on departure day


Wednesday’s 4 p.m. close can tempt travelers into a tight airport connection.1 A safer plan is to decide in advance which final visits are essential, where luggage will be stored, and when you need to leave McCormick Place based on live traffic, rail service, airline guidance, and airport conditions.


Before leaving the venue, photograph or digitize your handwritten notes, assign follow-up owners, and mark any claim that still needs validation. If the most important meeting is late Wednesday, you might consider departing Thursday so any needed outcome is not rushed.


The value of AHR Expo 2027 will come from the decisions made after the introductions and demonstrations. Choose a reliable winter route, protect time for the suppliers and sessions tied to active work, and capture evidence in a form your colleagues can use. FAQs


- AHR Expo 2027 runs Jan. 25–27 at McCormick Place, 2301 S. Martin Luther King Drive in Chicago. Published show hours are 10 a.m.–6 p.m. Monday and Tuesday and 10 a.m.–4 p.m. Wednesday.¹


- Both O’Hare and Midway have CTA routes to McCormick Place. O’Hare uses the Blue Line with a transfer to the Green Line; Midway uses the Orange Line with a transfer at Roosevelt to the Green Line.⁴ Compare the full route to your hotel, nonstop flight options, arrival time, and luggage before choosing.


- The organizer states that official show hotels receive free shuttle service to and from McCormick Place on show days.³ That is convention transport, not airport transport. Arrange the airport portion separately and verify your hotel’s current shuttle pickup details.


- Plan for a warm indoor show floor and potentially freezing outdoor conditions. January climate normals are a 31.6°F high and 18.8°F low, but they are not a forecast.⁵ Bring layers, a winter outer layer, and comfortable weather-resistant shoes, then check the current forecast before departure.


- Ask the exhibitor first. AHR’s published policy says photography and video of a booth, products, or personnel are not allowed without the exhibitor’s permission.¹
